questions.questionText: A sum of money doubles itself in 6 years at compound interest. In how many years will it become 8 times itself?
questions.explanation: Doubling takes 6 years at compound interest, so each further doubling takes 6 years. 8 = 2^3, hence 3 x 6 = 18 years.
questions.shortcut: At compound interest, the doubling time stays constant; 4x = 2 doublings, 8x = 3, 16x = 4.

questions.questionText: A sum of money doubles itself in 8 years at simple interest. In how many years will it become three times itself?
questions.explanation: Doubling means interest = P in 8 years, so interest per year = P/8. Tripling needs interest = 2P, i.e. 2 x 8 = 16 years.
questions.shortcut: Interest per year is constant: doubling takes n years, tripling 2n, quadrupling 3n.

questions.questionText: A sum of money becomes five times itself in 8 years at simple interest. What is the rate of interest per annum?

questions.shortcut: Rate = (multiple - 1) x 100 / years = 4 x 100/8.

questions.questionText: A sum of money becomes 3 times itself in 12 years at simple interest. In how many years will it become 5 times itself?

questions.questionText: A man borrows Rs 72000 at 5% simple interest per annum and lends it at 7% per annum. What is his total gain in 3 years?

questions.shortcut: Net gain = principal x (lending rate - borrowing rate) x time / 100.
